known_unresolved_titles: When an explicit RMB symbol prefixes a Chinese numeral without a trailing unit, `normalizeMoneyValueV4('¥四千')`, `normalizeMoneyValueV4('￥四千')`, and `normalizeMoneyValueV4('¥肆仟')` all return `unsupported`, although the token grammar accepts these forms and equivalent `RMB四千`, `人民币四千`, and `￥4000` values normalize to `4000.00`. The omitted-yuan handling recognizes only `RMB_NAME`, so include `¥/￥` in this parsing path to avoid dropping an unambiguous amount.

Fresh evidence beyond the separate yearless-payment and `到账` fixes is that their combination still fails: `王甲工资于1月15日到账` (and the corresponding `收到` form) returns false from `hasSupportedCandidateAttribution`, so runtime adds `source_relation_unresolved` to a valid `payment_date`. The new month/day grammar is used only by the payment-verb branch, while this receipt branch still requires a full `calendarDate`; allow the same bounded `monthDayPaymentDate` here without inventing a year.

Explicit rates written as `王甲月工资为400元`, `王甲日工资为400元`, `王甲小时工资为400元`, or `王甲计件工资为400元` fail `hasSupportedCandidateAttribution` even when the candidate declares the corresponding `rateUnit`. The downstream source-rate grammar already recognizes these finite prefix forms, but this role whitelist admits only alternatives such as `月薪`, `日薪`, `时薪`, and `每月`, so runtime adds `source_relation_unresolved` to otherwise unambiguous rates; align the attribution vocabulary with the supported prefix-rate grammar.
